page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.metal-32xl is a memory-optimized bare-metal server featuring 128 vCPUs across 64 physical Intel Xeon 6455B cores. Operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides dedicated CPU allocation with 2.0 threads per core. The processor includes a 60 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512. It is equipped with 1024.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core.

Benchmark results place this server in the top tier for multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 139,186.68 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 22,175.0. Its memory subsystem delivers exceptional throughput, achieving a top-tier read-only large block uncached bandwidth of 480.81 GB/sec and write large block uncached bandwidth of 213.95 GB/sec. Database performance is highly competitive, with Redis SET operations reaching 155.31 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring in the top 10%.

This bare-metal configuration does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, meaning storage must be provisioned externally, and it is not designed for GPU-accelerated workloads. However, the high resource density of 1 TB of DDR5 RAM combined with high-frequency Intel Xeon processors offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound, CPU-intensive enterprise workloads. The server is highly suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory data stores like Redis, high-performance computing, and intensive software compilation tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services r7iz.metal-32xl is a memory-optimized bare-metal server powered by a 128-vCPU Intel Xeon 6455B processor running at 3.9 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 1024.0 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, alongside a 50 Gbps baseline network speed. The server lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, but delivers top-tier performance across multi-core CPU benchmarks, memory bandwidth, and database operations. It achieves 155.31 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and ranks in the top 10% for Passmark database operations. This hardware profile is highly efficient for memory-intensive enterprise applications, large-scale in-memory databases, and high-performance computing workloads that require dedicated physical resources without virtualization overhead.
